M5_REMEDIATION.finding: §4.4's heading read 'Why the one asymmetry, derived and not chosen', and revision 5's commit message attached the same word to 'EXPECTED_BY_PROTOCOL: NO is BLOCKING pre-handover and INFORMATIONAL post-read'. The referent a reader takes is the LEVEL, and the level is not derived.
M5_REMEDIATION.reproduced_how: NOT adopted from the review. The derivation was rebuilt from the cited sources at their own text — protocol §2.2, §3, §1 P-7, §2.3 — with premises numbered, before any edit.
M5_REMEDIATION.asymmetry_direction: ENTAILED. §2.2 makes Plan the surface's only writer until handover and the named actor the writer after it; build copies and does no templating. The set of legitimate producers of an undecodable_text file is strictly smaller before handover than after, so the same bytes are an anomaly pre-handover and may be an ordinary artifact post-read. This is entailed and revision 6 continues to state it as entailed.
M5_REMEDIATION.blocking_level: POLICY CHOICE. The premises reach I4 — a PASS in that state asserts a guarantee the run cannot support — and stop. I4 eliminates the permissive reading of the UNSCOPED guarantee row; it does not select between (a) block, rc=1, rebuild from spec, and (b) enumerate under [UNCHECKED] as EXPECTED_BY_PROTOCOL NO, count separately, and narrow the pre-handover GUARANTEE_PROVIDED row. (b) is consistent with every premise §4.4 cites and is exactly what --post-read does with the same class. Nothing in §1, §2.2, §2.3, §3 or §4.3 selects between them.
M5_REMEDIATION.falsifier_run: Mirror's own WHAT_WOULD_CHANGE_MY_MIND — a clause at BASE_HEAD or at revisions 1–4 under which an unanticipated-but-allowlisted artifact must make the pre-handover command exit non-zero rather than be enumerated. Searched; there is none.
M5_REMEDIATION.i1_disjunct_verified: §3 forbids patching a failed surface; it does not forbid the source root carrying a non-UTF-8 text-suffixed file, and build copying that faithfully is what §3 protects. Empirically empty for BENCH-AB-001 today — 16 of 16 allowlisted text-suffixed files decode as UTF-8, measured — which is a contingent fact about this source root, not a normative exclusion. §4.4 now says so.
